title: Ares: High Performance Near-Storage Accelerator for FHE-based Private Set Intersection
problem: General-purpose FHE accelerators do not adequately address the unique requirements of Private Set Intersection applications, leading to suboptimal data handling, underutilization of hardware bandwidth, and inefficient deployment for PSI acceleration.
motivation: Privacy-preserving PSI based on FHE is widely deployed in federated learning and password verification, but inefficient FHE processing of large databases limits practical adoption.
method: Ares pairs a specialized FPGA (reconfigurable hardware chip) with custom software to accelerate Private Set Intersection (finding which elements appear in both encrypted datasets). It introduces Lazy Relinearization—postponing a standard encryption maintenance step that PSI operations normally execute repeatedly until multiple instances can be combined—reducing redundant work without changing the PSI protocol. The system analyzes PSI's computational patterns and implements them as optimized hardware circuits, ensuring the FPGA fully utilizes its bandwidth and processing power.
key_novelty: Lazy Relinearization defers a standard encryption operation in Private Set Intersection (finding common elements in encrypted datasets) to enable batching without protocol changes, paired with FPGA hardware architecture tailored to PSI's computational patterns.
contributions: Lazy Relinearization algorithm reducing PSI computational complexity
Analysis and decoupling of PSI computing patterns for efficient hardware mapping
47.99x speedup vs CPU; 1.79x-1.93x speedup vs SOTA FPGA accelerators (Poseidon, FAB)

metrics.speedup: 47.99x vs CPU, 1.79x vs Poseidon, 1.93x vs FAB

limitations: Not discussed; focus is on PSI-specific optimization.
primary_theme: PSI-specialized FHE accelerator with lazy relinearization optimization
